issues.description: Control frame stores a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service holds a mutable FrameProcessor instance, complecting a value-like control frame with runtime identity. This blocks serialization, retains swapped-out services, and forces equality semantics on object identity. Pass a stable service id or name string and resolve at the switcher edge.

issues.description: Targeting comparison via `==` on FrameProcessor relies on default identity equality and is fragile
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` depends on FrameProcessor's inherited __eq__. A future override, wrapper, proxy, or re-instantiation silently breaks routing and leaks the control frame downstream. Use `is`, compare by stable id, and state the invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Handler contract is split and unstated: services re-push, switcher suppresses on match
issues.detail: STTService now calls `_push_stt_metadata()` then `push_frame(frame)`, relying on the switcher to swallow it only when service matches active. The postcondition (frame invisible downstream, ordering of metadata-then-marker, behavior outside a switcher) is nowhere documented and creates LSP hazards for subclasses. Centralize re-push or document the contract on the frame and STTService.

issues.description: Inactive-target case is unspecified; frames targeting non-active services leak downstream
issues.detail: The suppression branch only fires when `frame.service == active_service`. Behavior for an inactive-target frame reaching push_frame is neither documented, asserted, nor tested. Today the dispatcher prevents it, but the invariant is implicit. State the postcondition for all target/state cases or assert-and-drop.

issues.description: Forward-reference annotation `"FrameProcessor"` without a TYPE_CHECKING import in frames.py
issues.detail: The dataclass annotates `service: "FrameProcessor"` as a string but FrameProcessor isn't imported in frames.py. Runtime works, but `get_type_hints`, schema introspection, pydantic adapters, and IDE tooling will fail to resolve it. Add a TYPE_CHECKING import or weaken the annotation honestly.

issues.description: Public rename lacks a deprecation alias for downstream importers
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was an exported symbol; renaming it outright breaks every downstream importer at the next version bump. A one-line alias plus a DeprecationWarning preserves back-compat at trivial cost. The changelog entry alone is insufficient.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the rename clarifies intent and the diff is small and focused, but the implementation reaches for the wrong data shape: a live FrameProcessor instance is embedded in a control frame and compared by default `==`, complecting value with identity and creating brittle targeting semantics. The handler contract is split across STTService (re-push after handle) and the switcher (suppress on match) without being written down, with unspecified behavior for inactive targets and outside-switcher use. Secondary concerns include an unresolved forward-reference annotation and a missing back-compat alias for the renamed public symbol. Recommend narrowing `service` to a stable identifier, documenting the handler contract and ordering invariant, and adding a deprecation alias before landing.
